identity.name: VINDHYA TELELINKS LTD
identity.sector: Telecom Infrastructure & Defense Communications Network Solutions

summary.oneLiner: Vindhya Telelinks Ltd is an integrated cable manufacturer and infrastructure EPC contractor, with EPC (telecom, water, irrigation, power) contributing 75.95% of turnover and cable manufacturing the balance.
summary.business: The Company operates two business segments: manufacture of telecommunication cables (jelly filled copper cables, optical fibre cables including high fibre count and ribbon OFC, solar PV cables, railway signalling and quad cables, power and specialty cables, FRP Rod/Glass Rovings and telecom fibre accessories) from its facilities at Rewa (M.P.), and Engineering, Procurement & Construction (EPC) turnkey services across telecom network rollouts (including IP-1), water supply, irrigation and sewerage, power distribution and substations, solar power plants, gas pipeline and system integration. Customers are largely B2B - central and state government departments, public sector undertakings, Indian Railways, telecom operators and private infrastructure players. The Company also owns IP-1 category passive optical fibre network infrastructure which it describes as a strategic asset.

Cable: Optical Fibre Cables (incl. high fibre count / ribbon OFC)
Industrial and other specialised connectivity solutions
EPC: Power distribution and substations (incl. gas insulated substation)

currentContext.expansion: Expansion in FY2025-26 was concentrated in the Cable business at Rewa (M.P.). Additions to fixed assets during the year were stated to be mainly for capacity augmentation of Solar PV Cables and other specialty cable infrastructure at the Rewa manufacturing facilities. The Company already has two E-Beam (Electron Beam) Irradiation facilities operational and is in the process of commissioning a third E-Beam facility, which it says is likely to be operational by the end of the first quarter of financial year 2026-27; the facility produces cables for solar renewable energy, rolling stock, electric vehicle and ship-wiring applications. Management describes these as 'ongoing capacity enhancement initiatives, including the expansion of E-beam irradiation facilities', expected to strengthen manufacturing capability and market reach in high-growth segments. Separately, to capture demand from the AI physical-infrastructure wave, the cable business segment is gradually expanding its manufacturing capacity of high fibre count ribbon optical fibre cable and other advanced specialty optical fibre cable products with increased capital outlay, and is 'gradually unlocking investment specifically for high fibre count optical fibre cables capacity to meet the demand growth'. On the EPC side there is no plant capex; expansion is footprint- and capability-led - the Company was awarded a power (gas insulated) substation project in the NDMC area of New Delhi during the year, is enhancing O&M capabilities, and plans to invest in automation, GIS mapping and digital tools for execution efficiency in power distribution and water infrastructure. The Company is also evaluating strategic opportunities from its IP-1 passive telecom infrastructure network spread across 23 states. A proposed amalgamation with a company in the same telecommunication cables and accessories business is intended to consolidate manufacturing capacities into a larger unified entity. No installed-capacity figures (MT, km or fkm) are disclosed anywhere in the routed text.

risks.risk: Dependence on government budgetary allocations and the timing of government payments, most acutely the Uttar Pradesh Jal Jeevan Mission
risks.note: Management's own first-listed risk is 'prevailing financial and liquidity conditions within the broader economy, including governmental budgetary allocations for key clients'. FY2025-26 showed exactly this: delays in fund releases under UP-JJM cut EPC revenue and impacted project execution, liquidity cycles and profitability, and the central JJM allocation was itself cut from an initial Rs 67,000 crore to Rs 17,000 crore mid-year on audit and procedural delays before being restored to Rs 67,670 crore. With EPC at roughly three-quarters of turnover, a single scheme's funding cycle drives the top line.

risks.risk: Working-capital intensity and receivable build-up in the EPC segment, and the finance cost it carries
risks.note: Trade receivables rose sharply over the year, attributed primarily to UP-JJM receivables after the budgetary cut, and finance costs increased primarily due to higher borrowings taken to fund increased working capital requirements. Management flags 'Liquidity risk due to current slowdown in government expenditure' as an explicit EPC risk and says the segment is focused on improving cash cycles and timely collections; recovery of substantial outstanding dues is expected only by end of the calendar year, so the exposure persists into FY2026-27.

risks.risk: Government EPC contracts largely lack price-variation or escalation protection, against volatile input costs
risks.note: The Directors' Report states that 'a significant portion of EPC contracts, particularly in the Government sector, continue to operate without adequate price variation or escalation protection mechanisms'. Volatility in steel, cement, copper, aluminium and petroleum derivatives, and fluctuations attributed to west Asia disturbances, therefore land directly on project margins. Management separately flags the 'potential inability to pass through to its customers increase in cost like labour, energy, etc.' as a risk to future profitability, and has responded by bidding selectively rather than by hedging the exposure away.

risks.risk: Turnkey project execution risk - delays, right-of-way and clearance constraints, and the penalties and cost overruns that follow
risks.note: Management lists 'potential delays in the execution of turnkey projects, leading to financial penalties and cost overruns' and, for the EPC segment, 'customary operational risks such as rights-of-way conflicts, resource availability challenges, and adherence to stipulated project completion timelines'. The Threats section adds execution delays from land acquisition, Right of Way constraints and local clearances. These are structural to a multi-state, government-client EPC book and are managed through pre-bid planning and execution monitoring rather than eliminated.

The related-party/segment note discloses that revenue from two customers was more than 10% of the Company's total revenue (a single customer exceeded 10% in the prior year). Combined with the EPC segment's reliance on a small number of large government schemes, this concentrates both revenue and collection risk in very few counterparties. (Read in the related-party note supplied in the governance bundle, not in the routed risks material.)

risks.risk: Intensifying competition and aggressive bidding compressing prices
risks.note: Listed twice by management - 'intensifying competitive dynamics within the marketplace' among the key risks, and in Threats as 'the entry of large, well-capitalized players and aggressive bidding practices may create pricing pressure, impacting profitability'. In a tender-driven EPC market with limited differentiation on price, this directly caps the margin the Company can bid for, which is why it has moved to prioritising order-book quality over volume.

risks.risk: Input supply and geopolitical supply-chain exposure, including constrained bare optical fibre and preform supply
risks.note: Management describes preform supply as genuinely constrained for the first time since 2018 with limited room for near-term capacity relief, feeding a sharp spike in bare fibre and cable prices, with manufacturers shifting capacity toward higher-value G657 A2 grades. It also flags growing global protectionism, supply chain disruption, regional conflicts and economic nationalism as forcing a reassessment of dependencies. The Company says it is 'relatively insulated to a significant extent' via a long-term agreement for uninterrupted optical fibre supply - a mitigant whose durability is itself the exposure.

risks.risk: Governance overhang: three wholly owned NBFC subsidiaries outside the consolidated accounts since April 2021, with books in dispute and litigation pending
risks.note: Form AOC-1 records that the consolidated financial statements for the year ended March 31, 2026 were prepared without the financial statements of August Agents Ltd., Insilco Agents Ltd. and Laneseda Agents Ltd., because validly approved financial statements have not been made available since April 1, 2021, ex-directors are stated to hold unauthorised and illegal possession of their books and records, and legal proceedings are pending before different courts. This leaves a five-year-old, unresolved gap in the consolidated picture whose eventual incorporation is undetermined. (Read in the AOC-1 material supplied in the governance bundle.)

themes.title: Telecom & digital-infrastructure capex
themes.need: 5G monetization, FTTH and tower/fibre densification drive the connectivity cycle - and Q1FY27 repriced the optical leg outright. STLTECH booked order intake of INR 13,100cr in ONE quarter, 1.7x its entire FY26 order book, anchored by a multi-year $1.1bn hyperscaler deal running through FY29, taking the open order book to INR 18,618cr (up 2.4x QoQ) on revenue of INR 1,910cr (+87%) and EBITDA INR 397cr (+184%). It then raised guidance twice on the same call - EBITDA margin target from 20%-by-end-FY27 (already hit at 20.8% in Q1) to 23%, and Data-Center + Enterprise mix from 30% to 50% of FY27 revenue, after DC went from 1% of revenue in FY26 to 21%. The catch is supply, not demand: ex the anchor deal quarterly intake fell to ~INR 3,000cr from INR 7,000-8,000cr because 'we have to pick and choose the orders basis the capacity availability', with germanium and helium named as binding raw-material constraints. BHARTIARTL on ARPU + 5G; INDUSTOWER on tower rollout; SUYOG-tier on passive infra; GTPL/HFCL-tier on broadband + fibre; tariff hikes and rural FTTH are the near-term levers.
themes.driver: STLTECH's $1.1bn hyperscaler ramp against germanium/helium supply constraints and the raised 23% margin / 50% DC-mix guides; tariff-hike flow-through; 5G/FTTH capex; tower tenancy adds.
